info.title: PEC Massiva 2.0
info.description: This service offers rest calls to send massive pecs and check the status of the delivery verification and receipt verification emails

get.description: Returns the status of the receipt and delivery verification emails relating to the sending with the code returned at the time of sending the PEC

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Code returned at the time of sending the PEC. Two accepted formats, with DIFFERENT response item shapes: a legacy date-based code starting with "20" (e.g. "2020082610003492"), or a 24-char unique id returned when the PEC was sent.

200.description: OK. Item shape depends on the code format used (see the code parameter): legacy "20..." codes return the ResponseStatus shape (sender/recipient/data/object/message); a 24-char ObjectId code returns a different shape instead (uid/messageId/sender/recipient/date/subject/body/attachmentCount/viaSubjectOnly, same items as readEmailByMessageId).

post.summary: Send a PEC and create a trackable thread
post.description:
Sends a PEC to the recipient(s) and creates a trackable thread: the returned threadId (== msgId for the newly created root) can be used with GET /threads/{threadId} to read the full thread, with PATCH /threads/{threadId} to add a reply, or with DELETE /threads/{threadId} to delete it. If the daily limit of 3500 sends is exceeded, the request is queued (status: pending) instead of being rejected. Supports an optional callback, invoked when the send completes and reused by PATCH /threads/{threadId} replies on this thread that don't specify their own. Always creates a NEW, independent thread — does not accept an id in the URL (use PATCH /threads/{threadId} to continue an existing one). Note: on the test server, the subject of the actually-sent email gets a " --- SANDBOX ---" suffix appended.
For testing, use the mailbox "username": "testsandboxpecmassiva@pecmassiva.com", "password": "openapitest" — a bold notice line stating it's a test send gets prepended to the body.

get.description: Returns the whole thread as a single chronological conversation: the original send (or every reply sent later via PATCH), merged with any PEC receipts and real replies found on the mailbox. Each entry is tagged direction: "out" (something this account sent) or "in" (something received). Entries still in queue (not yet sent) have no IMAP data attached. Each entry also reports attachmentCount (metadata only, no content — fetch a single message via GET /threads/{threadId}/{msgId} to download its attachments).

patch.description:
Sends a follow-up email on an existing thread: same sender/recipient as the root message, subject prefixed with "Re: " (no double prefix), email headers In-Reply-To/References pointing to the root Message-ID. Only body (+ optional attachments) and username/password are required — sender/recipient/subject are taken from the thread root. Follows the same daily-quota rule as POST /threads: over the 3500/day limit, the reply is queued instead of sent immediately. The thread root must already have been sent (a root still in queue cannot be continued). Supports an optional callback, invoked when the send completes (only for the immediate-send case — a queued reply's callback fires later, when the cron job actually sends it). If omitted, falls back to the callback configured on the thread's original POST /threads call, if any. Same test-server " --- SANDBOX ---" subject suffix caveat as POST /threads applies here too.
For testing, use the mailbox "username": "testsandboxpecmassiva@pecmassiva.com", "password": "openapitest" — a bold notice line stating it's a test send gets prepended to the body.

callback.description: Optional. Invoked with the same payload as the 200 response's data, once the send completes. If omitted, the thread root's own callback (from POST /threads) is used instead, if any.

delete.description: Deletes the thread root and every reply (records for pec_submissions/pec_queue), best-effort deletes the corresponding emails on IMAP (both INBOX and the Posta Inviata/Sent folder), and also deletes every received message (receipts and real replies) of this thread from INBOX plus their pec_inbound_refs records. To delete a single message instead of the whole thread, use DELETE /threads/{threadId}/{msgId}.

200.description: OK. deleted/skipped list BOTH the thread's own messages (root+replies, internal _id) and the received messages' internal ref ids (pec_inbound_refs) — an id is only in deleted if its email was actually removed from IMAP (or it was still queued, nothing to remove).

get.summary: Read a single message of a thread, with full attachments
get.description: Same entry shape as one item of GET /threads/{threadId}'s conversation, but with full attachment content (base64) instead of just attachmentCount. msgId is always a 24-char unique id (ObjectId). If it matches a message this account sent or queued (root or reply), attachments come from the encrypted bucket copy if still queued, or are re-parsed from the IMAP MIME structure of the Posta Inviata copy if already sent. Otherwise it's the internal ref (pec_inbound_refs) of a received message (receipt or real reply) — the actual IMAP uid is resolved internally from that ref, and attachments are re-parsed from the corresponding IMAP MIME structure. Ownership of the thread (x-username must match the thread's sender) and IMAP connectivity are checked before returning anything.

delete.summary: Delete a single message within a thread
delete.description: Deletes one message of the thread instead of the whole thread. msgId is always a 24-char unique id (ObjectId). If it matches a message this account already sent (root or reply), the email is deleted from IMAP first — if that fails, nothing is deleted and the record is kept. If it's still queued (never sent), only the record is removed, no IMAP involved. Otherwise msgId is the internal ref (pec_inbound_refs) of a received message: deleted from INBOX first, then its ref record — again, nothing is deleted if the IMAP deletion fails.

get.description:
Returns unread messages (IMAP \Seen flag not set) in your INBOX, most recent first (higher IMAP UID first), without marking them as read. For each unread message, attempts to resolve which PEC thread it belongs to by inspecting its headers only (X-Riferimento-Message-ID for standard receipts, In-Reply-To/References for real replies, subject match as a lower-confidence fallback for PEC-to-PEC replies wrapped in a transport envelope with no Message-ID linkage) — no message body is fetched, so checking never marks anything as read.
Note: a null threadId does not guarantee the message is unrelated to any thread — some replies are only identifiable by opening the full thread's conversation (which does fetch the body).

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of unread messages to skip, ordered most recent first. Default 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max number of unread messages to return. Omit for no limit (all unread messages).

id.description: IMAP UID of the unread message — use with GET/DELETE /inbox/{id}

threadId.description: Id of the matching /threads thread, or null if no cheap (header-only) match was found

msgId.description: Same msgId used when reading or sending on a thread. Null unless threadId was resolved and the message has a usable Message-ID header.

count.description: Number of items in data (this page)

total.description: Total unread messages in the mailbox, regardless of skip/limit

limit.description: Null if no limit was requested

Callback.description: Standardized callback configuration. Enables receiving notifications about status updates of asynchronous requests.

method.description: Specify the callback method. When set to 'POST', a standard HTTP POST request will be initiated with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded. The JSON data will be encoded into a key-value pair named 'data' (customizable via the 'field' parameter). When set to 'JSON', a direct HTTP POST request will be made with Content-Type application/json and the raw JSON body.

field.description: Works with method='POST'. Determines the name of the parameter sent in the POST request body. Null when method='JSON' (not applicable).

url.description: A valid URL capable of handling POST requests. For authenticated endpoints use the 'headers' parameter. Maximum timeout is 30 seconds. If 'retry' is set, the system retries until a 200 status code is received.

retry.description: Maximum number of retry attempts. Retries only on temporary errors (e.g. 502, 503) or network issues, with exponential backoff. Maximum value is 5.

headers.description: HTTP headers to send with the callback request. Useful for authentication (basic auth, bearer auth) or custom metadata.

custom.description: Additional data to include in the callback payload, accessible in the 'custom' key of the callback body. Can be any JSON value (object, array, string, number).

recipient.description: Send a mail to one or multiple recipients. This field accepts either a string or an array of strings.

username.description: Also used as sender (the two are always the same mailbox). Must end with @pecmassiva.com, OR belong to a mailbox registered with tipo_casella = PECMASSIVA.
